title: sampling-policy-matrix-and-widget-sizing-for-cohort-slis
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes for a sampling policy decision matrix and concrete widget sizing recommendations tied to cohort-level SLIs. This is an operational plan (not final) to guide instrumentation changes and dashboard refresh in Q1. The goal is to keep trace/query cost bounded while preserving signal for regression hunting and postmortems.

Background and constraints

- Telemetry budget: ~ $14k / month for traces and heavy analytics across prod and canaries.
- Product need: cohort-level 95th P99 latency SLIs for inference pipelines (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Operator need: fast RCA for token-path latency contributions and cold-cache incidents.
- Runtime: multi-tenant inference with routing, KV cache, batching. Traces are relatively large (avg 6 spans per inference path).

Key definitions (for this doc)

- Cohort: tenant or traffic slice we track SLIs for (e.g., free-tier webhooks, tier-A enterprise, internal-canary).
- Widget sizing: target row/card density on dashboards, and implied sampling resolution (how many points/minute).
- Sampling policy: rules applied at ingestion (probabilistic, severity-weighted, deterministic for canaries, head-only).

High-level goals

1) Ensure high-fidelity traces for failure windows and latency outliers.
2) Keep baseline sampling low-cost for long-term trend dashboards.
3) Enable tactical ramp-up (on-call-triggered) to capture ephemeral issues without changing instrumentation or deployments.

Decision matrix (short form)

Columns: trigger | sampling mode | retention tier | target widget sizing | notes

- Normal traffic | reservoir probabilistic 0.5% per tenant | standard-7d | 1 small tile per cohort (10-15 samples/hr) | low cost, long tail trends preserved
- High error rate (>= 0.5% above baseline) | severity-weighted + 10x | hot-30d | 1 medium tile per cohort (60 samples/hr) | capture error traces for RCA
- Latency spike detected (P95 > SLA) | head-only for that session + stochastic 5% for others | hot-14d | medium tile + trace-linking panel | preserve context around spike
- Canary traffic | deterministic 100% (for limited window) | hot-90d | wide detailed panel (multiple widgets) | required for rollout analysis
- Operator snapshot (manual) | tracing toggle (on-demand 100%) | ephemeral-3d | ad-hoc large tile / session detail | operator-initiated capture, no code change
- Sampling override (automated escalation) | rule-based ramp (0.5 -> 5% -> 20%) | hot-30d | escalate widgets to medium/large | automated by alerting playbook

Span & tag capture guidance

Essential spans (capture these at full fidelity where possible):
- request.ingest (receiving edge, tenant_id, api_key_hash)
- routing.route (chosen model variant, region, fallback info)
- queue.wait (queue time, priority class)
- batch.prepare (batch size, batch id)
- kvcache.lookup (hit/miss, prefix_key, warmth_hint)
- model.infer (model_name, seq_len, tokens_generated, quant_profile)
- postproc.format (tool-calls, function-calls, structured-output markers)

Preserve tags for grouping: tenant_id, session_id, trace_id, route_version, batch_id, is_canary, sample_decision. Redact PII upstream; use tenant hash instead of raw email.

Dashboard widget sizing recommendations (practical mapping)

- Small tile: one-timeseries, 15-min resolution, shows P50/P95/P99. Use for low-traffic cohorts. Keep sample rate low (0.5% or traces aggregated into histograms).
- Medium tile: timeseries + heatmap, 1-min resolution, include latency distribution and error-rate band. Target for mid-tier cohorts and canary groups.
- Large tile: trace-list + quick-links, per-session waterfall links, 10s resolution. For enterprise or elevated alerts, include raw traces.

Mapping sample rates -> widget expectations

- 0.5% reservoir -> baseline small tiles, histograms computed from metrics + occasional trace anchors.
- 5% probabilistic -> medium tiles with heatmaps and trace anchors for outliers.
- 20%+ or deterministic -> large panels with direct trace lists and waterfall links.

Alerting and escalation integration

- Alert: cohort P95 latency breach -> automatically increase sampling for that cohort to 5% for 60 minutes (rule executed by telemetry-ingestion lambda).
- Alert: error-rate surge -> severity-weighted sampling to capture all error traces for 30 minutes.
- Manual runbook: operator can push "trace-capture" annotation on an SLO incident to force 100% for a single tenant for 15 minutes.

Cost allocation heuristic

- Prioritize canaries and enterprise cohorts for trace budget.
- Hard cap set per-tenant: if tenant trace budget consumed, fall back to lower sampling and emit a budget-exhausted event.

Instrumentation checklist (developer handoff)

- Ensure spans listed above are emitted with stable names and semantic tags.
- Implement sample_decision tag on root span.
- Expose cohort label (tenant tier) on ingest so ingestion rules can act on it.
- Add feature flag to enable operator-initiated 100% capture per tenant.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs

- Do we keep model.infer at full payload size or only metadata (model_name, seq_len)? Full payloads increase trace size significantly.
- How long should deterministic canary traces live in hot tier vs cold archive? 90d may be high for cost.
- Should we prefer severity-weighted sampling over head-only for latency spikes (head-only preserves more contextual spans)?

Next steps (action items)

- Diego: prototype ingestion rule that ramps sampling for a cohort on P95 breach (ENGOBS-4123) — due 2026-03-10.
- Priya: draft dashboard wireframes for small/medium/large tiles and share in #observability for feedback by 2026-03-04.
- Liam: open PR with standardized span names and sample_decision tag (PR #89).
- Ava: run a 2-week cost simulation with synthetic traffic to validate $/month estimate and recommend caps by 2026-03-18.

Notes to self

- Keep debug-level logging of sampling decisions off in prod unless operator toggle is set.
- Cross-check archive retrieval path for trace linking in large incidents.

References and quick links

- Jira: ENGOBS-4123 (sampling ramp prototype)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/89
- Slack thread: #observability thread with sketches (see linked_artifacts)

End of draft.
